pages.title: Purification Scroll
pages.text: A single-use rite of absolution that responds only to a wearer of the Seal of Kadesh. It removes part of your Guilt and is the most direct relief while progressing Curse V.$(br2)Right-clicking also reduces Dynasty Threat by 100. The scroll is consumed only when it removes Guilt or Threat.

pages.title: Satiety Crystal
pages.text: Curse IX's bound debt token, created after the configured number of deaths, delivered after respawn and reissued if lost.$(br2)While wearing the seal, solve one inscription or eat any three different foods. Vanilla and modded foods can be mixed; each type counts once. Sneak-use or hover to view saved progress.$(br2)Either route consumes one crystal, repays one layer and restores the debt bar, hunger cap and attributes. Food repayment then seals inventory, hands, hotbar and interactions for a configurable 30 seconds. Items remain in place and unlock automatically. Remaining debt still drains, applying -99% attributes at zero.

pages.title: Ember of Duat
pages.text: Primarily found in Nether structure containers, with an extremely small chance to drop from hostile mobs.$(br2)It carries the inscription system, unlocks the Crown of Regency's reversal, and serves as a key to the final path.

pages.title: Heart of Duat
pages.text: The central combat relic of the midgame. It can awaken actively when enemies gather; otherwise, stacks of Battle Intent, stored mitigation, and environmental passives reward its wearer.$(br2)It marks the point where a victim of the curse begins wielding part of the dynasty's power.

pages.title: Resonant Scarab
pages.text: Awakened by playing the complete Hymn of the Two Lands. While worn, it grants resistance, attack, armor, and interaction-range bonuses. Removing it disperses the resonance and returns the scarab to sleep.

pages.title: Edict of the Two Lands
pages.text: A royal implement for the middle and late game that consumes Guilt to activate. Its ordinary Edict and Half-Dome Edict phases provide tactical control, displacement, and execution.
